items.title: SQLite foreign_keys pragma never enabled — declared cascade FKs not actually enforced
items.notes: Found 2026-07-20 by the BUG-33 schema brief. Original claim: src/backend/db/index.ts has no `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` anywhere, and plain SQLite disables FK enforcement by default per-connection — concluded that declared cascades were decorative only. CORRECTED 2026-07-20, same session: the BUG-32 backend brief independently hit this exact question (a real production 500 on deleting a place with items still referencing it — only possible if the FK constraint IS being enforced) and empirically verified via an isolated @libsql/client script that FK enforcement is ON by default with this driver, no explicit pragma needed. COO independently reproduced the same test directly (DELETE against a referenced parent row failed with SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_FOREIGNKEY) and confirms this. items.title: items.carriedFromItemId has no onDelete FK behavior — trip deletion 500s if a carried-forward item still references it
items.notes: Found 2026-07-21 by the WP-03/WP-04 Frontend brief (PR #208) while writing E2E coverage for the carried-forward tag — pre-existing defect, not introduced by that PR. Symptom: DELETE /api/trips/:id 500s if any of the trip's items was ever used as a carry-forward source (items.carried_from_item_id) for an item in ANY other trip, including trips since modified/locked/unlocked (the reference persists independent of trip status). Root cause: carriedFromItemId is a self-referencing FK (.references(() => items.id)) with no .onDelete(...) clause — SQLite/@libsql FK enforcement (confirmed ON by default, see BUG-38) defaults to RESTRICT. ARCHITECT RULING 2026-07-21 (ADL-36, jobs/architect/tech/20260307-architecture-decisions-log.md, GitHub issue #209, PR #212 merged): onDelete: 'set null' CONFIRMED (High confidence) — cascade rejected (would destroy an independent item on another trip), restrict is the bug. Verified safe against every current consumer: UpdateItemSchema does not expose the carry-forward fields (PATCH can't re-validate the coupling), the frontend tag reads the is_carried_forward boolean not the FK, no read path assumes carried_from_item_id non-null, and the partial index is already WHERE ... IS NOT NULL — NO backend/frontend change needed. The resulting is_carried_forward=1 / carried_from_item_id=NULL state is INTENTIONAL (create-time coupling per ADL-13 only; is_carried_forward is the permanent fact, the FK is a nullable provenance pointer). FK audit: BUG-39 is ISOLATED — every other no-onDelete FK references soft-deleted admin lists (never hard-deleted) or non-deletable geo/seed tables; items.tripPlaceId's omission is BUG-32's deliberate app-level reassign. No follow-up bug entry. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-21 (PR #214, merged, all 9 CI checks green): carriedFromItemId FK now onDelete: 'set null' in schema.ts; migration 0011_majestic_nehzno.sql generated via db:generate/db:migrate (never db:push) — table-recreation SQL eyeballed, self-FK ON DELETE SET NULL / partial index idx_items_carried / all 3 chk_items_* CHECK constraints / existing row data all confirmed intact. schema.ts doc comment updated recording the intentional post-deletion state. Regression test added (trips.delete.test.ts) asserting DELETE /api/trips/:id returns 204 (was 500) with the derived item surviving, carried_from_item_id nulled, is_carried_forward unchanged — self-verified against a reverted fix to confirm it's a real regression guard. Deleting an individual source item directly was confirmed to hit the same constraint, also fixed by this change. GitHub issue #209 (closed via PR #214). Full discovery write-up: jobs/frontend/park-docs/20260721-FRONTEND-wp03wp04-park.txt.

items.title: Agent read-only diagnostic access to Railway, Turso, Clerk (ADL-33)
items.notes: Operational tooling, no BRD ID (ADL-33 §8). Triggered 2026-07-21 by manual log-relay pain during a live Railway deploy debug session. Architect ADL-33: Turso GRANT (clean, DB-scoped read-only tokens); Railway GRANT WITH CAVEAT (no read-only token scope exists); Clerk DO NOT GRANT. PO confirmed both. IMPLEMENTED (PR #181, merged): Turso + Railway hosts added to init-firewall.sh; .env.agent-diagnostics (gitignored) with both Turso tokens (verified via JWT claim inspection — distinct per-database `rid`, not account/group-scoped, after an initial false start with a mistakenly-pasted account-level token, flagged for revocation, never used) and both Railway tokens (one per environment — PO provided one for each rather than prod-only; verified via GraphQL auth — distinct environmentId per token confirms real per-environment scoping). scripts/agent-diagnostics/turso-query.mjs and railway-query.sh (read-only query runners) + runbook. ALSO FOUND AND FIXED (ADL-34, same PR): init-firewall.sh fail-open bug — one dead static domain (statsig.anthropic.com, NXDOMAIN) aborted the whole script before the default-DROP lockdown was ever applied, leaving the container's outbound network fully unrestricted every container start. Fixed by moving lockdown before domain resolution. FIRST REAL USE (same session) surfaced the actual root cause of the original stuck-deploy problem: the Railway project's plan is `trial`, and Railway was actively deprioritizing Trial/Hobby deploys platform-wide during a demand spike (2026-07-21, confirmed via Railway status/community reports) — not a code/config issue. Flagged to Ryan: confirm the Hobby-plan upgrade from ADL-32 actually completed; Pro tier is the only tier that fully bypasses the deploy queue. FOLLOW-UP (2026-07-21, ADL-34 §5): the container rebuild happened and surfaced a second bug in the same fix — GitHub itself failed the final verification (`unable to reach https://api.github.com`). Root cause: lockdown-before-resolution now blocks step 6's own `curl https://api.github.com/meta` bootstrap fetch (chicken-and-egg — GitHub's IPs aren't allowlisted yet because that fetch is what's supposed to allowlist them). Fixed by DNS-bootstrapping api.github.com's IP via `dig` (same pattern as the Turso/Railway entries) before the curl call. VERIFIED 2026-07-22: Ryan rebuilt the container since this fix; the following COO session made dozens of successful `gh` CLI calls throughout (gh pr create/merge, gh issue create/close, gh run list/view, across ~10 PRs) with zero firewall/DNS errors — direct end-to-end confirmation the GitHub-bootstrap fix holds post-rebuild. items.title: test-db.ts hand-mirrors 21 CREATE TABLE statements — silent schema-drift risk in every repository test
items.notes: Logged 2026-07-26 (COO) during the OP-15 prerequisite audit. Was previously untracked — it existed only as a sub-bullet inside OP-15's notes ('Q22 test-DDL consolidation'), so deferring OP-15 would have buried it. src/backend/repositories/__tests__/test-db.ts imports db/schema.ts for Drizzle typing but then hand-writes all 21 tables as literal DDL. A migration can therefore change the real schema while every repository test keeps passing green against the stale copy — the tests would not detect the drift. Same family as the stale local dev.db that caused a false alarm during the 2026-07-26 BUG-63 investigation (companions missing user_id post-migration 0012). Count has grown from the 13 recorded in OP-15's notes to 21, so this is actively worsening. Fix direction: drop the hand-written DDL and apply the real migrations to the in-memory libSQL DB (migrate(db, { migrationsFolder: 'src/backend/migrations' })) so the test schema is identical to production's by construction. IMPLEMENTATION CAVEAT for the brief: createTestDb() runs in beforeEach across ~580 backend tests, so replaying 12+ migration files per test may hurt suite time — build the schema once and clone per test rather than re-migrating. Also clears OP-15 prerequisite (a); sequence this BEFORE the OP-15 skills design pass. Scheduled as batch B9 in jobs/COO/backlog-clearance-plan.md. DONE 2026-07-28 — B9, issue #291, PR #292. test-db.ts now applies the real migrations to a throwaway template :memory: DB, lifts the resulting DDL from sqlite_master (excluding __drizzle_migrations and sqlite_% internals), caches it at module scope, and replays it per test via client.batch() — so the schema is migration-derived by construction while paying the migration cost once, not per test. Suite runtime 6.75s -> 6.91s, noise-level. Drift detection DEMONSTRATED, not just asserted: adding a DROP COLUMN to migration 0012 made all 17 companions tests fail; before this change that same edit had zero effect on any repository test. Verified independently by COO against the diff. FOUND EN ROUTE: items.test.ts used status 'booked' in 8 places — never valid against chk_items_status and absent from all application code; the old CHECK-free hand-written DDL had masked it for the life of the file. Corrected to 'confirmed'. SCOPE LIMIT — see QUAL-17: this fixed test-db.ts only, and 15 further test files hand-roll the same DDL independently, so route-level tests are NOT yet drift-safe.

items.title: UK constituent countries (Scotland etc.) unavailable when adding a place
items.notes: Found 2026-07-20 UAT. Countries are ISO 3166-1 (countryCode is the PK, e.g. 'US','AU') — Scotland/England/Wales/Northern Ireland aren't countries under that standard, they'd be Regions under GB, same tier as US states/AU provinces (GE-01/02/06). GB appears missing from seed data entirely, or seeded without region_tier_enabled — either way this is a gap against GE-04/05 ('every country ships pre-configured, defaults applied automatically on first launch'). Fix: seed GB/'United Kingdom' with region_tier_enabled=1, region_tier_label likely 'Constituent Country', and add Scotland/England/Wales/Northern Ireland as regions. P1 — the Scotland dogfood trial (BRD-PL0104 trigger) needs this working. GitHub issue #154. DISPATCHED 2026-07-20 to database agent, branch fix/bug30-uk-region-seed. PR opened 2026-07-20: #168, Closes #154, all 9 CI checks green. Root cause: GB was present with region_tier_enabled=0. Fix: region_tier_enabled=1 + label 'Constituent Country', added England/Scotland/Wales/NI as regions (GB-ENG/SCT/WLS/NIR) via data-only custom migration, guarded to only patch already-seeded installs (self-caught a fresh-install idempotency bug in first draft — startup.service.ts seedRegions() would have been starved on a truly fresh install). Flagged: possible 5th drizzle-kit@0.31.9 bug (migrate CLI transiently dropped the new migration's journal entry once, not reproduced after) — noted in memory for future watching, not yet confirmed as a real/reproducible bug. MERGED to main 2026-07-20 (PR #168, squash), main CI confirmed green post-merge.

items.title: Time-varying CI checks must not gate deploys — Dependency Vulnerability Scan excluded from the production branch
items.notes: ADL-40 (2026-07-26). Trigger: production deploys blocked outright — `Security Checks` failed on production@299ab5c (run 30210259329) on GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6 (body-parser, HIGH), and Railway gates prod deploys on CI green. Root cause is NOT the promotion: `npm audit` queries the advisory DB at run time, so the identical tree passed on main 2026-07-24 and failed on production 2026-07-26 (verified — `git diff 299ab5c 3889436 -- package-lock.json package.json` is empty; only drift-ledger/STATUS.md/tracker.json/park-doc changed between them). Deployability had become a function of the calendar. Fix: security.yml push trigger `branches: ["**"]` → `branches-ignore: ["production"]`; ci.yml deliberately unchanged and still gates prod. Does not weaken security — check runs attach to a commit SHA not a branch, and production is only ever fast-forwarded from main, so every promoted SHA already carries this workflow's green statuses; the re-run is skipped, the verdict is frozen at the point it was earned. Detection unchanged on PRs and main (how DEP-01/DEP-02 were both found). Residual accepted gap: a direct push to production bypassing main would be unscanned — contained by process (CLAUDE.md: production is ff-only, agents never touch it). Alternative of removing Railway's CI gate entirely rejected by PO. Deferred idea, not adopted: a scheduled nightly audit on main that opens an issue, which would also catch advisories landing against an unchanged main between PRs. Production promoted to ce5dbd5 same session, CI + Security Checks both green, deploy gate reopened. security-backlog.md bumped to v1.3 with a pointer section, same PR.

items.title: Staging Railway environment ALLOWED_ORIGINS missing https:// scheme — CORS blocks all asset requests, white screen
items.notes: Found 2026-07-21, immediately after OP-22 closed. PO reported staging white screen + empty Turso DB. Diagnosed via read-only diagnostics (turso-query.mjs + Railway deploymentLogs GraphQL query, both per the ADL-33 runbook): Turso staging DB is fine (own separate instance, fully migrated 12/12, 250 countries seeded) — 0 users because nobody's ever gotten past sign-in. Root cause confirmed directly from server logs: `[ERROR] GET /assets/index-BGMSZVwk.css 500 CORS: origin 'https://travel-tracker-staging.up.railway.app' not allowed` (server.ts:122). Vite tags module scripts/stylesheets `crossorigin`, so the browser sends an Origin header on every asset request; CORS middleware does an exact string match against ALLOWED_ORIGINS, and the global error handler turns a rejection into a JSON 500 — browser sees wrong-MIME-type CSS + 500'd JS, i.e. white screen. EXACT ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by PO checking the Railway dashboard): Staging's ALLOWED_ORIGINS was set to the bare hostname `travel-tracker-staging.up.railway.app`, missing the `https://` scheme — `req.headers.origin` is always scheme-included, so the exact-match check in server.ts:119 never matched. FIXED 2026-07-21: PO added the `https://` scheme on the Railway dashboard and redeployed (deployment 12e1e764, 06:03 UTC). VERIFIED independently (not just PO's visual confirmation): new deployment's logs show zero CORS errors (vs. the prior deployment's immediate CORS rejection on every asset request); Turso staging `users` table now has 1 real row (`is_owner=0`, sign-in genuinely completed) — confirmed via turso-query.mjs, not just taking PO's word. CLOSED. Follow-on: this same verification pass surfaced BUG-60 (trust proxy / rate-limit misconfiguration, present in both prod and staging, unrelated to this fix).

items.title: Express 'trust proxy' not configured — express-rate-limit can't safely resolve client IPs behind Railway's proxy
items.notes: Found 2026-07-21 while verifying BUG-59's fix (deployment log review, both prod and staging). Railway sits its app behind a proxy that sets X-Forwarded-For; server.ts never calls `app.set('trust proxy', ...)`, so Express defaults to not trusting it. express-rate-limit (SEC-07, server.ts ~L147-153) detects this mismatch and throws `ERR_ERL_UNEXPECTED_X_FORWARDED_FOR` (see https://express-rate-limit.github.io/ERR_ERL_UNEXPECTED_X_FORWARDED_FOR/). CONFIRMED PRESENT IN BOTH ENVIRONMENTS via deploymentLogs: staging deployment 12e1e764 (06:05 UTC) and prod deployment f60d623b (05:45 UTC, i.e. already present in prod BEFORE any of today's changes — this is not something today's session introduced). Severity assessment: fires once shortly after boot in both environments' logs, not repeated per-request — consistent with the app being otherwise functional (prod 'confirmed working' 2026-07-21 shakedown, staging sign-in completed successfully today), so this is NOT currently a hard block on traffic. The real concern is correctness/security of SEC-07's rate-limiting: without an explicit, correctly-scoped `trust proxy` value, IP attribution behind Railway's proxy may be inaccurate (all traffic bucketed under one apparent IP) or spoofable (a forged X-Forwarded-For header trusted when it shouldn't be) depending on how this actually resolves at runtime — needs an Architect read on the correct value (e.g. `trust proxy: 1` vs Railway's actual proxy count/CIDR) rather than a guessed one-liner, since getting this wrong in the other direction (trusting an untrusted hop) is its own security hole. Per the standing project rule that runtime/infrastructure config changes need Architect ADL before COO acts — not fixed unilaterally. Affects both environments identically; one fix branch covers both once specced. RESOLVED 2026-07-22: ADL-37 — `app.set('trust proxy', 1)` (hop-count integer, not `true`; `true` would trust the whole X-Forwarded-For chain and let a client forge/spoof req.ip to bypass the rate limit, which express-rate-limit itself rejects as ERR_ERL_PERMISSIVE_TRUST_PROXY). Implemented in server.ts + mirrored in server-test-app.ts; new regression test (trust-proxy.test.ts) asserts the compiled trust predicate accepts hop 0 and rejects hop 1, not just the literal setting value. GitHub issue #221 (closed via PR #222, squash-merged, CI 9/9 green). VERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-22: Ryan approved promoting `main` → `production` (24 commits, incl. WP-01–04 Waypoint reskin + BUG-59) via the standard ADL-35 fast-forward; both envs redeployed (prod 8ca4c7fc, staging 4ff379e4) and their boot logs read clean via `railway-query.sh logs` — no ERR_ERL_UNEXPECTED_X_FORWARDED_FOR, no CORS errors, only an unrelated npm `production` config deprecation warning. CLOSED, both environments confirmed.

items.title: scripts/ci-wait.sh branch mode can PASS against the previous commit — races the mandatory post-merge main check
items.notes: FOLLOW-UP 2026-07-27 (PR #268). The first fix left an asymmetry: branch mode got a settle window for late-registering workflows, PR mode did not, because `gh pr checks --watch` was assumed to cover it. It does not — --watch returns once the checks it already knows about finish, and this repo's push + pull_request triggers register two sets at different moments. Observed live on PR #267 in the same session: ci-wait reported PASS on 9 checks, and the rollup showed 18 moments later. Benign in that instance (the late set is the identical job matrix on the identical commit, so only flakiness could differ) but it is the same fail-open shape the fix existed to close, and it was introduced by the fix rather than pre-existing. PR mode now re-watches while the check set is still growing. Deliberately, correctness does not rest on that loop terminating at the right moment: the authoritative rollup counts anything non-terminal as not-green, so an early exit yields a FAIL, never a false PASS — the loop only avoids spurious failures. ORIGINAL FIX: RESOLVED 2026-07-27 (PR #265). Branch mode now resolves the target commit from the branch itself (`gh api repos/<repo>/commits/<branch>`) instead of from run recency, then polls until runs exist for THAT SHA (bounded, DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT=180s) and exits non-zero if none ever register — 'no evidence' is now a failure, not a pass. A settle window re-queries after the first run appears so a late-registering second workflow (CI vs Security Checks) can't be missed. TIMEOUT is now an overall budget rather than a per-run allowance. CORRECTION to the original triage below: PR mode WAS affected too, by the same fail-open class — `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup` returns an empty array before any check registers, giving `length` 0 non-green and therefore PASS; separately the non-green filter excluded `conclusion == null`, so checks still queued were silently ignored. Both fixed: zero checks is now a hard failure, and a still-pending check counts as not-green. Also found while fixing: `gh api` ignores `--jq` on an error response and writes the raw error JSON body to stdout with a non-zero exit, so a resolved SHA that is merely non-empty can actually be an error blob — guards now validate the 40-hex SHA shape rather than non-emptiness. Verified with 7 tests incl. a forced-unregistered-commit harness proving fail-closed in both modes, and a structural check that the old script contained zero branch-tip lookups. ORIGINAL TRIAGE: GitHub issue #263. Found live 2026-07-26 during the QUAL-06 close-out. In branch mode, scripts/ci-wait.sh:79 resolves its target by taking `gh run list --branch <b> --limit 1 --json headSha` — i.e. whatever the LATEST RUN happens to be — then waits only for runs whose headSha matches that. Called immediately after a merge, before GitHub has registered workflow runs for the new commit, the latest run is still the PREVIOUS commit's, which is already complete and green. It prints 'PASS — all runs green for main @ <old sha>' and exits 0 without ever waiting for the commit the caller cares about. Observed exactly this: returned PASS @ 89ad005 seconds after merging PR #262, while main was actually at 1b84557 with both CI and Security Checks still in_progress. Re-running ~30s later correctly waited and passed @ 1b84557. Severity is P1 because this is the enforcement mechanism for CLAUDE.md's MANDATORY post-merge verification ('a green PR does not guarantee a green main', BUG-24) — the one check standing between a squash-merge race and an unnoticed red main. It fails open: a genuinely red main would be reported green if the check is run promptly after merging, which is exactly when the procedure says to run it. Caught here only because the printed SHA was read rather than just the PASS. Fix direction: branch mode should take the expected SHA rather than inferring it — e.g. accept an optional SHA argument, or derive `git rev-parse origin/<branch>` after a fetch — and POLL UNTIL RUNS EXIST for that SHA (with a timeout) instead of treating 'no runs yet' as 'use the latest run'. Note ci-wait.sh:89 already has a 'No runs found for the latest commit' branch, so the not-yet-registered case is partly anticipated; the defect is that the SHA itself is inferred from run history rather than from the branch tip. PR-mode (`ci-wait.sh pr <n>`) is not affected — it resolves runs from the PR, not from run recency.

items.title: GitHub Actions pinned to v4 target Node.js 20 — deprecated, force-run on Node 24
items.notes: GitHub issue #266. Surfaced 2026-07-27 while reading main's CI logs during the BUG-64 verification (PR #265) — every job emits 'Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24: actions/checkout@34e1148..., actions/setup-node@49933ea...'. Both are SHA-pinned to v4 across 16 call sites: .github/workflows/ci.yml (8x checkout, 6x setup-node) and .github/workflows/security.yml (3x checkout, 1x setup-node). P3 rather than P2 because GitHub is ALREADY force-running these on Node 24 and they pass, so runtime compatibility is empirically proven rather than assumed; the residual risk is only that GitHub eventually errors instead of forcing, which would break CI entirely. Long runway, low effort, no current breakage. Success criteria: (1) both actions at v5 across all 16 call sites; (2) SHA pinning PRESERVED — pin the v5 commit SHA with a trailing '# v5' comment matching the existing convention, do not switch to floating tags (the pinning is a deliberate supply-chain control); (3) the deprecation warning no longer appears in any job log; (4) all CI + Security Checks green on the PR and main green after merge. items.title: Assert PRAGMA foreign_keys=1 at startup (remote Turso path verified 2026-07-28)
items.notes: Raised 2026-07-27 by ADL-41/S1 (issue #271, §11). NOT a live defect — S1 probed the installed @libsql/client and found foreign keys are ON by default (a libSQL divergence from stock SQLite), so declared ON DELETE CASCADE is genuinely enforced and TR-14's delete works as designed. This entry is the guard, not a fix: createLibSQLDb (src/backend/db/index.ts:119) issues no PRAGMA of its own, so the behaviour rests entirely on a client default that a future version bump could change silently, and every cascade in the schema depends on it. Asserting it at startup converts a silent data-integrity regression into a loud boot failure. REMOTE-TURSO HALF ANSWERED 2026-07-28 (COO): S1's premise that 'this container's firewall blocks every Turso host' was FALSE — the ADL-33/OP-21 diagnostic path is allowlisted. Probed staging via scripts/agent-diagnostics/turso-query.mjs and PRAGMA foreign_keys returns 1. Confirmed genuinely remote (libsql://...turso.io + auth token; the script has no file-URL fallback and exits if the URL is absent), so this is not a local-driver result misread as remote. Per ADL-41 §7.2's own transport analysis this reading is stronger than it looks: each statement is independently dispatched on the remote HTTP transport, so a PRAGMA read reflects the per-statement server default — the exact condition every cascade executes under. RESIDUAL: this is a pragma read on a read-only connection, not a behavioural test that an FK-violating write is rejected; the diagnostic token is read-only by design and the script refuses non-SELECT, so the conclusive version needs write credentials this environment lacks. That residual does not block the assertion. DISPATCH DECISION 2026-07-28 (PO): the assertion rides along with the B9/QUAL-03 backend brief rather than dispatching separately — same backend/test-infrastructure surface, ~15 lines plus a test. Implementation note from ADL-41 §7.2: assert (read), do NOT set — issuing PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON at connect looks like a fix and guarantees nothing on the remote transport. Success criteria: startup asserts PRAGMA foreign_keys=1 on the real application connection and fails loudly if not; remote verification recorded (done — see above).

items.title: Concurrent role dispatches collide on the single shared jobs/<role>/context/current.txt
items.notes: Found 2026-07-27 during the Wave 0 merge round, flagged by ADL-41/S1. jobs/architect/context/current.txt is ONE file and all five Wave 0 Architect briefs instructed the agent to update it, so concurrent dispatches collide there by construction. Worktree isolation does not help — it is a genuine same-file, same-region conflict. Three of the four merges hit it and were resolved by hand, keeping every session's block; S1 pre-empted it by prepending rather than clobbering, which is the only reason nothing was silently lost. Left unresolved it is a data-loss shape, not just friction: git auto-merge CAN succeed by taking one side, and the last PR merged would silently win. Note the ADL log did NOT conflict in any merge — the pre-assigned-number + rewrite-your-own-stub-in-place design worked exactly as intended, so the contrast points at the fix. Options: per-dispatch context files (current-<brief>.txt), an append-only format with a required section header per session, or dropping the 'update current.txt' instruction from concurrent-wave briefs entirely. Success criteria: a wave of >=3 concurrent same-role dispatches produces no manual conflict resolution in the context file.

items.notes: Found 2026-07-28 alongside QUAL-15, while sweeping the same init lists for broken paths. All 8 role prompts say 'Read _shared/frameworks.txt' as init step 1, and TWO different files answer to that name: /_shared/frameworks.txt (8397 bytes, 'SHARED FRAMEWORKS' — the 30 numbered binding standards covering coding, communication, quality, security SEC rules 19-22, spec review 23-24, and bug classification 25-30) and /jobs/_shared/frameworks.txt (1562 bytes, 'TRAVEL TRACKER — SHARED TECH STACK' — languages, frameworks, versions, env vars). They are not duplicates of each other; they are unrelated documents that collide on filename. From the repo root, which is where a worktree-isolated agent starts, the bare path resolves to the 30-standards doc — which is probably the intended one, since /coo-startup references 'Shared Standards 23/24' as living in _shared/frameworks.txt. So current behaviour is likely correct and no agent is reading nothing. But an agent reading the prompt from jobs/<role>/ could reasonably resolve it the other way, and the tech-stack doc is genuinely useful at init too. Success criteria: init step 1 names its target(s) by explicit path from the repo root — probably both files, since both are relevant — so there is no resolution ambiguity; consider renaming one file if the collision is worth removing outright.

Success criteria: the 15 files derive their schema from the same migration-driven helper as test-db.ts; no hand-written CREATE TABLE remains in any backend test file; a deliberate migration change is detectable by route-level tests as well as repository tests; backend suite stays green with no material runtime regression.

items.title: Semgrep job pulls semgrep/semgrep:latest unpinned from Docker Hub
items.notes: Found 2026-07-27 when main went red immediately after PR #270 merged: the Security Checks / Static Analysis (Semgrep) job failed because the runner could not reach Docker Hub (registry-1.docker.io: context deadline exceeded, 3 retries) and the container never started. Not a code failure — Semgrep had passed on the identical tree 20 minutes earlier, and a re-run passed. TWO distinct concerns from one incident: (1) FLAKINESS — this is the only external runtime dependency in either workflow that is not SHA-pinned, and a registry blip turns main red for reasons unrelated to the code, which under CLAUDE.md must then be diagnosed and fixed immediately rather than left; (2) SUPPLY CHAIN — 'latest' means the analysis container can change under us with no review, while every GitHub Action in the same workflows is deliberately SHA-pinned (see DEP-03, which treats that pinning as a control worth preserving). The inconsistency is the argument. PENDING PO DECISION: raised with Ryan twice on 2026-07-27, no answer given either time — log it or leave it. Logged here rather than dropped so the question survives the session. CLOSED 2026-07-28 (PO): leave as-is, revisit only if it recurs. Two findings from the COO analysis that preceded the decision, both of which undercut this entry's original framing and must be read before anyone reopens it. (1) PINNING THE IMAGE DOES NOT PIN THE ANALYSIS. Four of the job's five --config values (p/typescript, p/react, p/nodejs, p/owasp-top-ten) are Semgrep Registry rulesets fetched over the network at scan time; only .semgrep/security.yml is local. So the job has TWO external runtime dependencies, not one, and digest-pinning the image pins the engine while leaving the rules floating. The genuinely worrying supply-chain case here is not a malicious image but rules silently disappearing and dropping scan coverage with no signal — which pinning does not touch. (2) 'ADD A RETRY' IS NOT AVAILABLE AS A CHEAP FIX. This is a job-level container: (.github/workflows/security.yml:77-78); if the image pull fails the job dies before any step runs, so there is no step for a retry action to live in. Retry-ability requires restructuring the job so Semgrep is installed within a step (e.g. pip install on a normal ubuntu runner), which also moves the dependency from Docker Hub to PyPI and allows a pinned version. IF IT RECURS, the right fix is that restructure — NOT digest-pinning, which addresses neither the observed availability failure nor rule drift and buys only cosmetic consistency with the SHA-pinned actions/*. Observed rate at closure: one incident in the project's history.
